    <h1>Decay of the Higgs boson</h1>
  </header>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
Consider the decay of the Higgs boson into a fermion pair $f\bar{f}$.

The quantum state of the fermions has the form $$|f\bar{f}\rangle = \int \frac{d\boldsymbol{p}_1}{(2\pi)^3\sqrt{2E_1}}\frac{d\boldsymbol{p}_2}{(2\pi)^3\sqrt{2E_2}}\widetilde{\psi}(\boldsymbol{p}_1,s_1;\boldsymbol{p}_2,s_2)|f(\boldsymbol{p}_1,s_1),\bar{f}(\boldsymbol{p}_2,s_2)\rangle,$$ where $\widetilde{\psi}$ is the two-particle wave function of the fermions in the momentum representation and $s_i$ are the spin 4-vectors. In the rest frame of a fermion $s=(0,\boldsymbol{\xi})$.

- Find $\widetilde{\psi}$ using the matrix element $$\langle f(\boldsymbol{p}_1,s_1),\bar{f}(\boldsymbol{p}_2,s_2)|S-1|H\rangle.$$ ✓  Now compute the wave function in the coordinate representation: $$\psi(\boldsymbol{x}_1,\boldsymbol{x}_2) = \int \frac{d\boldsymbol{p}_1}{(2\pi)^3}\frac{d\boldsymbol{p}_2}{(2\pi)^3}\widetilde{\psi}(\boldsymbol{p}_1,s_1;\boldsymbol{p}_2,s_2)e^{+i\left(\boldsymbol{p}_1\cdot \boldsymbol{x}_1+\boldsymbol{p}_2\cdot\boldsymbol{x}_2\right)}.$$ Show that $\psi(\boldsymbol{x}_1,\boldsymbol{x}_2)$ depends on the difference of the coordinates $\boldsymbol{r}=\boldsymbol{x}_1-\boldsymbol{x}_2$ and compute the wave function $\psi(\boldsymbol{r})$.

- Expand the wave function in spherical harmonics and study how it depends on $\boldsymbol{\xi}_1\cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{r}}$, $\boldsymbol{\xi}_2\cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{r}}$, $\boldsymbol{\xi}_1\cdot\boldsymbol{\xi}_2$. Interpret the result.

:::
